newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS - Indices slow post expiration.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS - Indices slow post expiration.

text.p: Trading in stock index options suffered from a post-expiration hangover on Monday despite whipsaws in the market, traders said.
"We haven't really had much volume," said one options trader. "We had an excellent Friday expiration, but it's very, very slow here today."

By 1445 CDT (1945 GMT), the spot S&P 100 index was down 5.69 points at 684.31 after rising to a record 692.67. The broader S&P 500 index was off 2.63 points at 708.19. It had reached a record high of 714.10 earlier.
At the same time, the bellwether Dow industrial average was down 19 points at around 6,075 after rising to about 6,134, also a record intraday high.

On the OEX, put volume topped call volume in the November series in action one options strategist said was likely due to people hedging against a market decline after the November 5 U.S. presidential election.
"They'll use any excuse for a selloff after the election," said Michael Schwartz at Oppenheimer & Co.
The most active OEX option was the November 680 put, which traded nearly 13,000 contracts. Its open interest was about 9,800 contracts.
The option was trading at its high for the day, 8-1/2, up 1-5/8 after falling to 5-5/8 on the market's morning rally.
Other busy OEX puts included the November 685 and 690, which traded more than 8,100 contracts each.
Among the OEX calls, the November 700 was most active, with nearly 5,900 contracts changing hands. It had open interest of 5,650.
No OEX option beyond the November expiration traded more than 1,000 contracts.
In SPX options traded on the Chicago Board Options Exchange, put volume outpaced call volume by 35,228 to 11,635 at 1400 CDT (1900 GMT).
Most of the put volume was seen in the November 700, 705, 710 and 715 strikes. The heaviest call activity was in the November 720, which traded 3,580 contracts.
The SPX December 695, 715 and 735 puts were also active, with 2,450, 1,300 and 2,350 contracts traded, respectively.

In the September 1997 series, investors were putting on positions in the 650, 675 and 700 puts. The September 650 put, with open interest of 2,350, traded 1,075 contracts. The 675 put, with open interest of 1,545, traded 1,150 contracts and the 700 traded 1,425 contracts. Its open interest was roughly 2,635 contracts.
